name: India
description: Subcontinental cradle of profound spiritual philosophies, mathematics (zero and decimal systems), magnificent rock-cut cave temples, grand dynastic empires, and global maritime trade.

kingdoms.title: Gupta Empire (Classical Golden Age)
kingdoms.description: The Golden Age of ancient India marked by monumental advancements in mathematics (the concept of zero and decimal system), astronomy, Sanskrit literature, and Hindu-Buddhist art.

kingdoms.title: Imperial Chola Dynasty
kingdoms.description: Dominant maritime empire of South India renowned for bronze sculpting, grand Dravidian stone temples (Brihadisvara), and naval expeditions across Southeast Asia.

kingdoms.title: Maurya Empire
kingdoms.description: First pan-Indian empire founded by Chandragupta Maurya and philosopher Chanakya, reaching its moral and philosophical pinnacle under Emperor Ashoka the Great.

kingdoms.title: Mughal Empire
kingdoms.description: Cosmopolitan Indo-Persian Islamic empire renowned for administrative unification, religious synthesis under Akbar, and peerless architectural masterworks like the Taj Mahal.

kingdoms.title: Vijayanagara Empire
kingdoms.description: Southern Indian empire that patronized fine arts, literature, and monumental temple architecture, creating a bustling commercial metropolis at Hampi.

kings.title: Ashoka the Great
kings.biography: Ashoka was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty, who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE. He promoted the spread of Buddhism across ancient Asia.

sections.heading: Biography
content: After the brutal Kalinga War, Ashoka renounced violence and embraced Buddhism.
He established a welfare state, built hospitals for people and animals, and erected pillars with edicts promoting morality.

kings.title: Chandragupta Maurya
kings.biography: Founder of the Maurya Empire with guidance from his guru Chanakya (Kautilya). Defeated Seleucus I Nicator and unified the Indian subcontinent from Bengal to Afghanistan under centralized rule.
kings.internationalConnections: Concluded a treaty of alliance with Seleucus I Nicator, welcoming Greek ambassador Megasthenes to Pataliputra.

kings.title: Emperor Ashoka the Great (Devanampriya Priyadasi)
kings.biography: Renowned pan-Indian emperor who, remorseful after the conquest of Kalinga, converted to Buddhism and dedicated his reign to Dhamma (righteousness), erecting the Pillars of Ashoka and sending Buddhist peace missions worldwide.
kings.internationalConnections: Sent royal peace missions to Ptolemaic Egypt, Hellenistic Greece, Antiochus II of Syria, and dispatched Mahinda and Sanghamitta to Sri Lanka (Devanampiya Tissa).

kings.title: Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar the Great
kings.biography: Third Mughal emperor who tripled the empire's size through military strategy, abolished the sectarian jizya tax, patronized interfaith dialogues at the Ibadat Khana, and created the syncretic Din-i Ilahi.
kings.internationalConnections: Exchanged embassies with Safavid Persia, the Ottoman Empire, and the Portuguese court in Goa.

kings.title: Rajaraja Chola I the Great
kings.biography: Visionary king who transformed the Chola kingdom into an extensive maritime empire. Conducted land surveys, built a formidable navy, and constructed the colossal granite Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur.
kings.internationalConnections: Sent naval expeditions to northern Sri Lanka and established diplomatic trade missions to Song Dynasty China.

kings.title: Samudragupta (Napoleon of India)
kings.biography: Great military ruler and patron of the arts recorded on the Allahabad Pillar. Conquered numerous kingdoms across the subcontinent while mastering poetry, music (playing the veena), and Vedic scholarship.
kings.internationalConnections: King Meghavanna of Sri Lanka sent envoys with gifts to Samudragupta requesting permission to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya.

kings.title: Shah Jahan (King of the World)
kings.biography: The master builder of the Mughal Empire who commissioned the Taj Mahal in Agra as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, as well as the Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Delhi.
kings.internationalConnections: Employed master European and Persian stonemasons, architects, and jewelers in the imperial workshop.

sites.name: Brihadisvara Temple (Big Temple of Thanjavur)
sites.description: Colossal 66-meter Dravidian granite temple dedicated to Shiva, one of the Great Living Chola Temples.
sites.history: Built by Rajaraja Chola to celebrate his imperial military conquests across South India and the Indian Ocean.
sites.construction: Constructed entirely of interlocking granite blocks without mortar, capped by a single 80-tonne granite dome (Kumbam) lifted via a 6 km earthen ramp.
sites.architecture: Features a 16-story pyramidal vimana tower, a colossal monolithic Nandi bull carved from a single stone, and vibrant Chola fresco paintings.
sites.significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987; the crowning triumph of South Indian architecture.
sites.currentStatus: Active place of worship and protected monument in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India.

sites.name: Ellora Caves & Kailasa Rock Temple
sites.description: Cave 16 (Kailasa Temple) is the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world, carved vertically downward from a solid basalt cliff.
sites.history: Showcases 34 major monasteries and temples representing Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions carved side by side in religious harmony.
sites.construction: Over 200,000 tonnes of basalt rock were chiseled away from top to bottom by hand over generations without scaffolds.
sites.architecture: Full-scale Dravidian temple standing two stories high, adorned with life-sized elephant statues, columned mandapas, and mythological bas-reliefs.
sites.significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983; an unparalleled feat of rock engineering.
sites.currentStatus: Standing pristine in Aurangabad District, Maharashtra, India.

sites.name: Great Stupa at Sanchi
sites.description: One of the oldest stone structures in India commissioned by Emperor Ashoka, featuring intricate torana gateways illustrating Buddhist jatakas.

sites.name: Hampi (Group of Monuments at Vijayanagara)
sites.description: Spectacular 4,100-hectare boulder-strewn capital city featuring over 1,600 surviving monuments, palaces, and hydraulic royal baths.
sites.history: The capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, described by Portuguese and Persian visitors as one of the richest metropolises in the world.
sites.construction: Engineered with local granite boulders, sophisticated aqueducts, and chariot shrines.
sites.architecture: Features the Virupaksha Temple, the stone chariot of the Vittala Temple with musical pillars, and the Lotus Mahal.
sites.currentStatus: Preserved archaeological complex in Bellary District, Karnataka, India.

sites.name: Taj Mahal
sites.description: Peerless white Makrana marble mausoleum on the Yamuna river, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
sites.history: Commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan to house the remains of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal. Built over 22 years by an army of 20,000 artisans under the direction of court architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori.
sites.construction: Crafted from translucent white Makrana marble inlaid with 28 varieties of precious and semi-precious stones (pietra dura technique) and flanked by red sandstone mosques.
sites.architecture: Flawless bilateral symmetry, a central double dome rising 73 meters, four detached minarets angled outward, and a formal Charbagh Persian paradise garden.
sites.significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007 and described by Rabindranath Tagore as 'a teardrop on the cheek of eternity.'
sites.currentStatus: Standing pristine and protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.
sites.wonderHistoricalContext: Declared an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007, recognized worldwide as the pinnacle of Indo-Islamic architectural symmetry and devotion.
